# Glossary

<!-- Generated by assaywatch.site_render from GLOSSARY.md. Edit that file. -->
!!! info "Reproduced verbatim from the repository's `GLOSSARY.md`"
    These are the terms used in the source code, comments and commit
    messages, rather than a separate vocabulary written for this site.
    Edits to
    [`GLOSSARY.md`](https://github.com/batyanight/assaywatch/blob/main/GLOSSARY.md)
    propagate here.
    Terms are cross-linked: the first mention of another defined term in a
    definition links to it (272 links).
    `assessable`, `coverage`, `drift`, `exclusion`, `exclusivity`, `flag`, `panel`, `site`, `status`, `target` are defined by more than one entry and so
    deliberately not linked.

The project's own vocabulary. Use these words, exactly, in function and variable names,
comments, commit messages and conversation. Definitions are taken from `config.yaml`,
`assaywatch/schema.py` and module docstrings; the location is given where the repo defines
the term precisely. PCR basics are not defined here. Add a term here before inventing a new
word for a concept.

## Registry and assays

**assay**{: #term-assay } — one registry entry: one published [primer](#term-primer) set (plus optional [probe](#term-probe)) with its target, [chemistry](#term-chemistry) and [citation](#term-citation), stored as one YAML in `registry/` (`schema.py` `Assay`).

**oligo**{: #term-oligo } — any single oligonucleotide of an [assay](#term-assay): forward [primer](#term-primer), reverse primer, [probe](#term-probe) or an alternate (`schema.py` `Oligo`).

**primer**{: #term-primer } — a forward or reverse [oligo](#term-oligo); scored by its distance from the 3' end.

**probe**{: #term-probe } — the internal [oligo](#term-oligo) of a `hydrolysis_probe`, `mgb` or `lna` [assay](#term-assay); absent in `conventional`, `sybr` and `rpa` assays (`assaywatch validate registry` prints the current split, which is not quoted here because a hand-written count goes stale; `config.yaml scoring:` for how a probe is scored).

**chemistry**{: #term-chemistry } — the [assay](#term-assay)'s [detection](#term-detection) format, one of `conventional`, `sybr`, `hydrolysis_probe`, `mgb`, `lna`, `rpa`; scoring overrides are keyed on it (`schema.py` `Chemistry`, `config.yaml scoring: by_chemistry`).

**amplicon**{: #term-amplicon } — the [product](#term-product) between the facing forward and reverse sites in a record.

**amplicon_bp**{: #term-amplicon-bp } — the [amplicon](#term-amplicon) length in bp, measured from where the primers sit on real GenBank records, never copied from the paper (`CLAUDE.md` "Measure, never quote").

**amplicon_bp_range**{: #term-amplicon-bp-range } — `[min, max]` declared for an [assay](#term-assay) whose [product](#term-product) length genuinely varies by species; mutually exclusive with `amplicon_bp` (`schema.py`).

**species_sizes**{: #term-species-sizes } — measured [product](#term-product) length per species, only valid alongside `amplicon_bp_range` (`schema.py` `SpeciesSize`).

**amplicon_disagrees_with_paper**{: #term-amplicon-disagrees-with-paper } — [review flag](#term-review-flag): the measured [amplicon](#term-amplicon) length differs from the published one, and the registry keeps the measured value (`CLAUDE.md`, `review.py`).

**target**{: #term-target } — the taxon and gene the [assay](#term-assay) is for: `taxid`, `taxon_name`, `gene`, `genome_type`, optional `query` (`schema.py` `Target`).

**gene name**{: #term-gene-name } — `target.gene`: `symbol (product)`, or a bare name where there is no separate symbol, each virus keeping its own true symbol (influenza NP, paramyxovirus N). Coordinates, accessions and ortholog lists go in `notes_curator`, unless a position is the locus's only identity.

**scope_taxids**{: #term-scope-taxids } — taxa the [assay](#term-assay) is meant to [detect](#term-detect); a record counts toward the drift denominator when its taxid or any ancestor is listed (`schema.py` `Target`, `config.yaml drift: scope_taxonomy`).

**exclusivity**{: #term-exclusivity } — a published claim that the [assay](#term-assay) does not amplify certain off-target taxa; those taxa are listed in `target.exclusivity_taxids`, retrieved on purpose, and reported as predicted cross-reactivity, never scored (`schema.py` `Target`).

**citation**{: #term-citation } — the paper an entry rests on (`schema.py` `Citation`); every live entry cites its own paper.

**doi_verified**{: #term-doi-verified } — `true` only after `scripts/resolve_citations.py` and `scripts/check_citations.py` have confirmed the DOI against Crossref; a DOI is always entered as `false` first (`CLAUDE.md`).

**status (active, draft, deprecated)**{: #term-status } — registry status, the entry's lifecycle; only a maintainer sets `active`, and an entry in `registry/` must also carry `doi_verified: true` (`schema.py` `Status`).

**pending entry**{: #term-pending-entry } — an [assay](#term-assay) YAML waiting for a verified DOI; it sits in `pending/`, is never screened, and is checked with `python -m assaywatch.validate pending --pending` (`CLAUDE.md`).

**review flag (needs_review)**{: #term-review-flag } — a controlled-vocabulary tag on an entry that can be filtered on, e.g. `oligos_read_from_figure`, `not_screenable`, `thin_evidence`; the specifics of one case go in prose, not the flag (`review.py`).

**nested protocol**{: #term-nested-protocol } — a nested or semi-nested protocol, stored as one entry per [round](#term-round), each screened as an independent [assay](#term-assay) and then cross-warned (`nested.py`).

**conditions**{: #term-conditions } — the thermal and reagent protocol exactly as the paper prints it (annealing temperature, salts, [oligo](#term-oligo) concentrations, `master_mix`); nothing in it is screened (`schema.py` `Conditions`).

**master mix**{: #term-master-mix } — the commercial reaction mix named in the paper, stored as the free-text `Conditions.master_mix` field; keep the term, it is the reagent's name.

**performance**{: #term-performance } — what the paper measured (LOD, efficiency, R squared, dynamic range); reported, not scored (`schema.py` `Performance`).

**panel**{: #term-panel } — one [inclusivity](#term-inclusivity) or exclusivity validation panel the paper ran, as counts `n_tested` and `n_detected` (`schema.py` `Panel`).

**use_context**{: #term-use-context } — free-text list of the settings an [assay](#term-assay) is used in; the intended use that the `drift.detect_fraction_threshold` comment says the right threshold depends on.

## Screening and scoring

**screen**{: #term-screen } — match every [oligo](#term-oligo) of an [assay](#term-assay) against every record of an [archive](#term-archive) and write one [call](#term-call) per (assay, record) (`screen.py`).

**call**{: #term-call } — the per-record outcome of a [screen](#term-screen) for one [assay](#term-assay), one of `detect`, `reduced`, `fail`, `indeterminate`, `no_amplicon` (`score.py` `Call`).

**detect**{: #term-detect } — a [call](#term-call): the summed [penalty](#term-penalty) is at most `scoring.detect_max` (`config.yaml scoring:`).

**reduced**{: #term-reduced } — a [call](#term-call): amplifies but with [penalty](#term-penalty) above `detect_max` and at most `reduced_max`; drift counts it as detected unless the [assay](#term-assay)'s [chemistry](#term-chemistry) is in `drift.reduced_not_detected_for` (`config.yaml`).

**fail**{: #term-fail } — a [call](#term-call): both primers land but the [penalty](#term-penalty) exceeds `reduced_max`, or a [terminal mismatch](#term-terminal-mismatch) fails it (`terminal_mismatch_fails`).

**no_amplicon**{: #term-no-amplicon } — a [call](#term-call): no facing [primer](#term-primer) pair in the right orientation within the [amplicon](#term-amplicon) size range. Kept out of the drift fraction, with one exception: a `no_amplicon` whose exclusion is `diverged` is counted as a failure under `drift.count_diverged_as_fail` (shipped `true`) (`drift.py`, `score.py`).

**indeterminate**{: #term-indeterminate } — a [call](#term-call): too many [undetermined](#term-undetermined) record bases (ambiguity codes, N) under an [oligo](#term-oligo) to score; kept out of the drift fraction (`score.py`).

**detection**{: #term-detection } — the predicted outcome that a record would amplify, i.e. a `detect` or (unless excluded) `reduced` [call](#term-call); drift's numerator is the detected share.

**not detected**{: #term-not-detected } — a `reduced` [call](#term-call) counted as not detected for the chemistries in `drift.reduced_not_detected_for` (currently `hydrolysis_probe`, `mgb`), where a [reduced](#term-reduced) [probe](#term-probe) call stops counting as a find (`config.yaml drift:`).

**evaluable record**{: #term-evaluable-record } — a record in the drift denominator: one with a `detect`, `reduced` or `fail` [call](#term-call), plus a `diverged` `no_amplicon` record under `drift.count_diverged_as_fail`. `indeterminate` and every other `no_amplicon` are not [evaluable](#term-evaluable-assessable-coverage-gap) (`drift.py`). See also **assessable** and **[coverage gap](#term-evaluable-assessable-coverage-gap)**, two further thresholds on the same count.

**exclusion**{: #term-exclusion } — the reason a record yielded no [amplicon](#term-amplicon): `no_site`, `truncated`, `diverged`, `no_pair`, or `chance_only` (`score.py classify_exclusion`).

**site**{: #term-site } — a binding site: a position in a record where an [oligo](#term-oligo) binds with at most `max_mismatches_searched` mismatches, found on both strands (`match.py`).

**penalty**{: #term-penalty } — the position-weighted [mismatch](#term-mismatch) cost of one [oligo](#term-oligo); forward, reverse and [probe](#term-probe) penalties are summed into one budget under the shipped `engine: budget` (`config.yaml scoring:`).

**3' window**{: #term-3-window } — the last `primer_3prime_window` (5) nt at a [primer](#term-primer)'s 3' end, penalized by `primer_3prime_penalty` per [mismatch](#term-mismatch) (`config.yaml scoring:`).

**mid window**{: #term-mid-window } — positions 6 to 10 from the 3' end, penalized by `primer_mid_penalty` per [mismatch](#term-mismatch) (`config.yaml scoring:`).

**5' region**{: #term-5-region } — the rest of a [primer](#term-primer), penalized by `primer_5prime_penalty` (`config.yaml scoring:`).

**terminal mismatch**{: #term-terminal-mismatch } — a [mismatch](#term-mismatch) at the 3'-most base of a [primer](#term-primer); with `terminal_mismatch_fails: true` it makes the [call](#term-call) `fail` regardless of identity (`config.yaml scoring:`).

**mismatch**{: #term-mismatch } — a position where an [oligo](#term-oligo) base and the record base it faces share no possible base; a degenerate oligo base that includes the record base is a match, and an [undetermined](#term-undetermined) record base is **[ambiguous](#term-ambiguous)**, not a mismatch (`iupac.py base_state`).

**mispair**{: #term-mispair } — the identity of a [mismatch](#term-mismatch) (template base : [primer](#term-primer) base, e.g. `G:T`), as opposed to its position; `mispair_penalty` overrides the cost of named mispairs such as G:T wobble (`config.yaml scoring:`, `score.py`).

**mispair window**{: #term-mispair-window } — how many bases from the 3' end `mispair_penalty` applies; null means `primer_3prime_window` (`scoring.mispair_window`).

**oligo verdict**{: #term-oligo-verdict } — under `engine: serial` only, the per-oligo judgement `ok`, `weak` or `blocked` set by `oligo_ok_max` and `oligo_weak_max` (`score.py oligo_verdict`). The only place "[verdict](#term-verdict)" means something other than a drift status.

**engine (budget, serial)**{: #term-engine } — how [oligo](#term-oligo) penalties combine: `budget` sums them against `detect_max`/`reduced_max`; `serial` judges each oligo alone and the worst decides (`scoring.engine`).

**degeneracy**{: #term-degeneracy } — the pool size of a degenerate [oligo](#term-oligo) ([product](#term-product) of its ambiguity-code multiplicities); reported with `tiers` negligible, moderate, high, never penalized (`degeneracy.py`, `config.yaml degeneracy:`).

**degenerate base**{: #term-degenerate-base } — an IUPAC ambiguity code written in an [oligo](#term-oligo), synthesised as a mixture; inosine is kept in `seq_as_written` (`iupac.py`, `schema.py`).

**ambiguous (record base)**{: #term-ambiguous } — a record position whose true base is [undetermined](#term-undetermined) (an IUPAC code or N in the record); the code also writes "undetermined" for the same thing; reported separately and never scored as a [mismatch](#term-mismatch) (`match.py`).

**chance pair**{: #term-chance-pair } — a forward and reverse site that face each other in [amplicon](#term-amplicon) range by chance in a long record, with nothing to do with the target (`chance.py`).

**E-value (site, pair)**{: #term-e-value } — expected number of such sites or pairs by chance in a record of that length and composition; `max_site_evalue` and `max_pair_evalue` set the credibility cut (`chance.py`, `config.yaml scoring:`).

**locus identity**{: #term-locus-identity } — whether an [amplicon](#term-amplicon)'s interior resembles the interiors of the amplicons the [assay](#term-assay) actually works on, the chemistry-independent form of the probe-site test; shipped off (`locus_identity_min: null`) (`locus_identity.py`, `config.yaml scoring:`).

**thermo**{: #term-thermo } — optional nearest-neighbor duplex Tm and delta Tm columns per [oligo](#term-oligo); shown, never scored, shipped `thermo: false` (`thermo.py`, `config.yaml`).

**footprint**{: #term-footprint } — one record's [mismatch](#term-mismatch) pattern for an [assay](#term-assay) (positions from the 3' end and ambiguity counts per [oligo](#term-oligo)), interned to a single string; millions of records share a few thousand footprints (`drift.py FOOTPRINT_COLUMNS`, `calls.py`).

**strategy**{: #term-strategy } — a pre-registered candidate scoring change, one YAML in `strategies/` overriding `config.yaml` values and carrying its own kill criterion, replayed against frozen sets.

**S-ladder (S0, S3b, S7, ...)**{: #term-s-ladder } — the numbered ladder of candidate scoring strategies; `S0` is the shipped rule, names are reserved in `docs/journal/2026-10-24-scoring-strategy-test-plan.md` (S5 is C2, the gated Bayesian per-record model) (`ROADMAP.md`).

## Drift and verdicts

**drift**{: #term-drift } — a fall over time in the share of GenBank records for a taxon in which an [assay](#term-assay)'s oligos still match; not the same as loss of infections detected (`config.yaml` "WHAT DRIFT IS AND IS NOT").

**baseline**{: #term-baseline } — the pooled earlier records an [assay](#term-assay)'s [recent window](#term-recent-window) is contrasted with (`drift.py`).

**deposit date**{: #term-deposit-date } — the day a record first appeared in GenBank (`created` in the metadata; esummary `CreateDate`, or an [assembly](#term-assembly)'s `release_date`); the clock every [verdict](#term-verdict), [window](#term-window) and [trend](#term-trend) runs on (`calls.read_dates`).

**collection date**{: #term-collection-date } — the day the isolate behind a record was collected, as BioSample gives it (a full date, a year-month, a bare year, a range or "missing"); carried for [assembly](#term-assembly) records only, in the `collected` metadata column and, for older archives, in the title (`assemblies.py`, `metadata.collection_year`).

**collection-year lens**{: #term-collection-year-lens } — the report section that re-dates each record by its collection YEAR and recomputes the recent share beside the deposit-clock one; a lens on sequencing backlog that moves no status (`report.collection_lens_rows`; decided 2026-10-30, `docs/journal/2026-10-30-design-grilled.md` Q1-Q3). [Assembly](#term-assembly) records only until `report.collection_sidecar` names the file `scripts/backfill_collection_dates.py` fetched; then every record.

**recent window**{: #term-recent-window } — the latest `recent_window_months` (24) of deposit dates, widened a year at a time up to `max_window_months` (60) when records are scarce (`config.yaml drift:`).

**status (drift)**{: #term-status-2 } — the per-assay drift [verdict](#term-verdict): `declining`, `low coverage`, `watch`, `insufficient data`, `no recent data`, `stable`, plus `no data` (`drift.py` `STATUS_ORDER`, `NO_DATA`; `docs/screening-and-the-drift-call.md` "The drift [call](#term-call)"). Not the registry **status (active, draft, deprecated)**; say "drift status" or "registry status" wherever both could be meant.

**declining**{: #term-declining } — status: recent share is below `detect_fraction_threshold`, the fall is at least `min_decline` with a [Newcombe interval](#term-wilson-newcombe-interval) wholly below zero, and the [assay](#term-assay) cleared the threshold in some earlier year (`drift.require_working_baseline`) (`docs/screening-and-the-drift-call.md`, `config.yaml drift:`).

**low coverage**{: #term-low-coverage } — drift status: below threshold but not measurably lower than before, or never working; an [assay](#term-assay) used beyond its design, or one that was always poor (`docs/screening-and-the-drift-call.md`). A pooled, over-time statement about one assay; not a cell of the **[coverage map](#term-coverage-map)**, which is per species and has no time axis.

**watch**{: #term-watch } — drift status: below threshold with an interval that still covers it (`docs/screening-and-the-drift-call.md`).

**insufficient data**{: #term-insufficient-data } — status: fewer than `min_records_for_drift` [evaluable](#term-evaluable-assessable-coverage-gap) records; reported, never flagged (`config.yaml drift:`).

**flag**{: #term-flag } — in drift, an [assay](#term-assay) whose recent upper [Wilson](#term-wilson-newcombe-interval) bound falls below the threshold (`flag_rule: wilson`) or whose posterior probability of being below it exceeds `flag_posterior_credibility` (`posterior`). Not a [review flag](#term-review-flag).

**detect_fraction_threshold**{: #term-detect-fraction-threshold } — share below which an [assay](#term-assay) is called failing, 0.90; a judgement about tolerable surveillance loss (`config.yaml drift:`).

**lineage**{: #term-lineage } — a group of records of one [assay](#term-assay)'s target defined by NCBI taxid (grouped at `group_at_rank: species`), so a miss on one clade is not averaged away (`lineage.py`, `config.yaml lineage:`).

**sublineage**{: #term-sublineage } — a finer split within one taxid, resolved from titles or by sequence-homology clustering (`cluster`, Mode C) where the taxid carries no label (`subcluster.py`, `clustermaps.py`, `config.yaml lineage: sublineage`).

**lineage-conditional verdict**{: #term-lineage-conditional-verdict } — the assay-level [verdict](#term-verdict) overridden when any one [lineage](#term-lineage) is significantly below threshold after Holm correction (`lineage.multiple_testing`), so the worst lineage drives the [call](#term-call) (`lineage.py`, `config.yaml lineage:`).

**site drift**{: #term-site-drift } — which [oligo](#term-oligo) positions are failing and in which [footprint](#term-footprint) groups of accessions, for assays the main report calls [declining](#term-declining) (`sitedrift.py`).

**trend**{: #term-trend } — a Cochran-Armitage test for a monotone slide in the detected share by deposit year, reported beside the [verdict](#term-verdict), never folded into it (`trend.py`, `config.yaml drift: trend_min_years`). Printed twice since 2026-10-30: by record (an upper bound on the evidence, since duplicated deposits count as independent) and **by [footprint](#term-footprint)** (each distinct footprint counted once per year; nearer a lower bound, since a sequencing error in a [primer](#term-primer) site mints a footprint). When they disagree on direction the report says so.

**hierarchical layer (C1)**{: #term-hierarchical-layer } — Beta-binomial [partial](#term-partial) pooling of an [assay](#term-assay)'s lineages; reported, never a [verdict](#term-verdict) unless `verdict_from: posterior` (`hierarchical.py`).

**Wilson / Newcombe interval**{: #term-wilson-newcombe-interval } — Wilson score interval for a proportion; Newcombe hybrid-score interval for a difference of two, built from the two Wilson intervals (`interval.py`, `drift.py`).

## Coverage

Agreed 2026-11-10. Coverage and drift are two separate summaries of the same calls table
and neither depends on the other; coverage is the primary product. Built the same day as
`assaywatch coverage` (`coverage.py`): the map, the cell states, recommendations and the
nested rows. NOT built yet, and marked below: the **locus check**, **widened retrieval**
and the **host column**'s data.

**coverage**{: #term-coverage } — which species an [assay](#term-assay) is predicted to [detect](#term-detect) as of today, including species outside what its paper claimed. A snapshot with no time axis. Bench vocabulary would say "in-silico [inclusivity](#term-inclusivity)"; this project says coverage.

**coverage map**{: #term-coverage-map } — the [assay](#term-assay) x species table: one **[coverage row](#term-coverage-row)** per species, one **[coverage cell](#term-coverage-cell)** per (assay, species).

**coverage row**{: #term-coverage-row } — one NCBI species taxid. Host never defines a row. A row is split by **[sublineage](#term-sublineage)** only where one taxid is known to hide distinct lineages (Bd, influenza A subtypes).

**host column**{: #term-host-column } — the hosts named in a row's records (the GenBank `/host` qualifier, shown as written, most common first). Displayed, never used to group or score. "Fish ranavirus" is something a reader concludes from this column; the tool does not claim it. Empty on real runs until retrieval stores `/host`.

**in-scope row / out-of-scope row**{: #term-in-scope-row-out-of-scope-row } — a row whose taxid is, or is not, under the [assay](#term-assay)'s `scope_taxids` (or its `target.taxid` where no scope is declared). Both are screened and shown, in separate blocks. Drift uses scope to shrink its denominator; coverage uses it only as a label.

**widened retrieval**{: #term-widened-retrieval } — a [retrieval group](#term-retrieval-group) fetched above the [assay](#term-assay)'s own target (typically the family) so out-of-scope species are in the [archive](#term-archive) at all. A per-assay retrieval setting. Not built: a species has a row today only if its records were already in the assay's archive.

**coverage cell**{: #term-coverage-cell } — the predicted outcome for one [assay](#term-assay) on one species, one of `predicted detect`, `partial`, `predicted fail`, `not assessable`, always printed with its **[cell count](#term-cell-count)**. No minimum record count hides a cell.

**cell count**{: #term-cell-count } — detected records over locus-present records for the cell, e.g. `8/10`. The reader judges a `3/3` and a `300/300` differently; the tool does not hide either.

**predicted detect**{: #term-predicted-detect } — cell state: the records carry no [mismatch](#term-mismatch) that would block the reaction. Worded that way on purpose. It says the oligos match; it does not say the reaction works.

**partial**{: #term-partial } — cell state: either the records split between detected and not, or they are detected with an expected loss of efficiency (e.g. one [mismatch](#term-mismatch) under a standard hydrolysis [probe](#term-probe): amplifies, expect a Ct shift). Not the per-record [call](#term-call) `reduced`, which is one input to it. In numbers (`config.yaml`, `coverage:`): more than `fail_max_share` detected and less than `detect_min_share` [cleanly detected](#term-cleanly-detected).

**cleanly detected**{: #term-cleanly-detected } — a record called `detect`. "Detected" in a [cell count](#term-cell-count) also includes `reduced`; `predicted detect` is judged on the cleanly detected share alone, so a species whose records are all `reduced` reads `partial` with a full count.

**predicted fail**{: #term-predicted-fail } — cell state: the locus is present and the oligos are predicted not to amplify it. A stronger claim than `predicted detect`, because a 3' [terminal mismatch](#term-terminal-mismatch) or a missing site is good evidence from sequence alone.

**not assessable**{: #term-not-assessable } — cell state: no record of that species is shown to contain the locus, so the [assay](#term-assay) was never tested by the data. Not a failure. Distinct from **assessable** (a drift [lineage](#term-lineage) with enough [evaluable](#term-evaluable-assessable-coverage-gap) records).

**locus check**{: #term-locus-check } — (not built) the test, independent of the primers, of whether a record contains the [assay](#term-assay)'s target region: a tolerant alignment of a [reference amplicon](#term-reference-amplicon) against the record. Decides between `predicted fail` and "does not count" when no [primer](#term-primer) site is found.

**locus present**{: #term-locus-present } — a record shown to hold the [assay](#term-assay)'s target region; only these enter a [cell count](#term-cell-count). Until the [locus check](#term-locus-check) exists the only evidence is the [screen](#term-screen)'s own: both primers found a site (a `detect`, `reduced` or `fail` [call](#term-call)) or the screen labelled the record `diverged`. So a distant species in which neither [primer](#term-primer) lands is invisible to the map.

**reference amplicon**{: #term-reference-amplicon } — an [amplicon](#term-amplicon) cut from a record the [assay](#term-assay) detects, used as the query of the [locus check](#term-locus-check).

**recommendation**{: #term-recommendation } — for one species, the assays ordered by [coverage cell](#term-coverage-cell), ties broken toward the less degenerate [primer](#term-primer) pool. A ranking, not a [verdict](#term-verdict).

**degeneracy annotation**{: #term-degeneracy-annotation } — the [degeneracy](#term-degeneracy) [tier](#term-tier) shown on an [assay](#term-assay)'s rows. It never changes a [call](#term-call) or a cell; it breaks ties in a [recommendation](#term-recommendation).

**nested rows**{: #term-nested-rows } — the three rows a nested or semi-nested protocol gets in the [coverage map](#term-coverage-map): **[together](#term-together)**, **[round 1 alone](#term-round-1-alone-round-2-alone)**, **[round 2 alone](#term-round-1-alone-round-2-alone)**. The two "alone" rows are the rounds' own registry entries; only `together` is computed, under the id `<last round's id>@together`.

**together**{: #term-together } — nested row: the protocol as published, [round](#term-round) 1 then round 2. Round 1 is scored on the **[trace rule](#term-trace-rule)**, round 2 on the normal rule, and the cell is the worse of the two.

**round 1 alone / round 2 alone**{: #term-round-1-alone-round-2-alone } — [nested rows](#term-nested-rows): that [round](#term-round)'s [primer](#term-primer) pair on raw template, scored on the normal rule because it carries the whole reaction. Round 2 alone is the fallback when round 1 misses a species.

**trace rule**{: #term-trace-rule } — the looser scoring of [round](#term-round) 1 inside a `together` row: round 1 only has to make a trace of [product](#term-product), so it fails only on a 3' [terminal mismatch](#term-terminal-mismatch) (one the scoring config does not price at zero) or no site (`coverage.trace_passes`). Agreed in outline 2026-11-10 and not measured. It is permissive: on the 2026-11-01 calls it lets nearly every scored round-1 record through, so a `together` row reads close to [round 2 alone](#term-round-1-alone-round-2-alone).

## Pipeline and runs

**retrieve**{: #term-retrieve } — fetch nucleotide records for a [retrieval group](#term-retrieval-group) from NCBI and [archive](#term-archive) them, incrementally (`retrieve.py`).

**retrieval group**{: #term-retrieval-group } — a (taxid, `target.query`) pair; assays sharing both share one [archive](#term-archive), on disk at `data/retrieved/<taxid>/<slug>/` (`retrieve.py`, `groups.py`).

**archive**{: #term-archive } — the gzipped FASTA plus `*.meta.tsv.gz` for one [retrieval group](#term-retrieval-group), keeping whole records so rescreening at any setting is free (`windows.py`, `retrieve.py`).

**assembly (`asm` group)**{: #term-assembly } — a [retrieval group](#term-retrieval-group) of sampled bacterial genome assemblies (`assemblies.taxa`, `per_year`) cut down to the loci the oligos could build an [amplicon](#term-amplicon) in, used where gene-level deposits stopped (`assemblies.py`).

**window archive**{: #term-window-archive } — an [archive](#term-archive) cut down to a `buffer_bp` [window](#term-window) around the sites a [screen](#term-screen) found, for distribution (`windows.py`).

**composition window**{: #term-composition-window } — one record's [amplicon](#term-amplicon) plus up to `flank_bp` of flank each side, every [primer](#term-primer)/[probe](#term-probe) site masked to N, cut by `subcluster.flanked_region` and returned as a `Region` with the flank actually used. What composition clusters; not a [window archive](#term-window-archive), which is cut around sites for distribution and keeps them.

**title token**{: #term-title-token } — a word a cluster's record titles carry and the other clusters' do not, shown in the composition panel's tooltip: what the cluster's name leaves out (`composition.title_tokens`). Record qualifiers (`strain`, `isolate`, `clone`) are never tokens.

**same-mix line**{: #term-same-mix-line } — an [assay](#term-assay)'s per-year detected share recomputed on the whole period's [lineage](#term-lineage) mix, by direct standardisation (`composition.same_mix_series`). Drawn beside the observed line: where the two diverge, the mix of lineages being deposited moved rather than [detection](#term-detection) within them.

**mix part / within part**{: #term-mix-part-within-part } — the two numbers Kitagawa's decomposition splits a change in detected share into: how much the [lineage](#term-lineage) mix moved, and how much [detection](#term-detection) moved within the lineages (`composition.split_change`). They add to the change exactly. A lineage deposited in only one of the two periods has no within part, so its whole effect is mix.

**new since design**{: #term-new-since-design } — of a species under an [assay](#term-assay)'s target taxon: first deposited in this assay's [archive](#term-archive) after the year its paper designed it (`composition.species_years`), so the designers could not have had it. Unset where the entry carries no `citation.design_year`.

**diverged stratum**{: #term-diverged-stratum } — in the composition panel, the records whose primers both landed past the [mismatch](#term-mismatch) budget: they have no [amplicon](#term-amplicon) and so no [composition window](#term-composition-window), and are drawn and counted as a [lineage](#term-lineage) of their own rather than placed by guesswork (`composition.DIVERGED`). Under `drift.count_diverged_as_fail` they are in the denominator, which is why the panel must show them.

**manifest**{: #term-manifest } — the [retrieve](#term-retrieve) stage's run state: per-group last-run dates and counts, kept as state not as a Snakemake output (`retrieve.py`, `timing.py`).

**run record**{: #term-run-record } — what `retrieve` returns for one fetched group (`TaxonRun`), written to the [manifest](#term-manifest) (`retrieve.py`).

**screen signature**{: #term-screen-signature } — the record, written beside a cached [screen](#term-screen), of what it was produced under, so `collect` can [detect](#term-detect) a stale screen whatever Snakemake remembers (`signature.py`).

**rescreen**{: #term-rescreen } — re-run `screen_archive` over the archives after a scoring or code change; the shipped scoring hash forces one (`config.yaml scoring:`, `signature.py`).

**collect**{: #term-collect } — gather the cached per-archive screens into one [calls table](#term-calls-table), `calls.tsv.gz` (`collect.py`).

**calls table**{: #term-calls-table } — `results/<date>/calls.tsv.gz`, one row per ([assay](#term-assay), record) (`calls.py`).

**taxa cache**{: #term-taxa-cache } — `docs/taxa-cache.json`, the [lineage](#term-lineage) analysis's taxid-to-name map (`config.yaml lineage.taxa_cache`); not the taxon records.

**taxon record**{: #term-taxon-record } — an entry in `docs/taxon-records.cache.json`: NCBI scientific name, common name and rank for a taxid, used by the [assay](#term-assay) sheet (`docs/assay-sheet.md`).

**pipeline stages**{: #term-pipeline-stages } — Snakefile rules `validate`, `retrieve`, `screen_archive`, `collect_calls`, `report`, `site_drift`, `lineage_analysis`, `degeneracy_table`, `figures`; `all` requests the outputs (`Snakefile`).

## Evidence and curation

**retrospective case**{: #term-retrospective-case } — a row in `docs/validation-cases*.tsv`: a published follow-up where an [assay](#term-assay) worked or failed, with its mechanism (`coverage` or `drift`); the evidence the thresholds are checked against (`config.yaml` header).

**development set**{: #term-development-set } — `docs/validation-cases.tsv`, the cases thresholds were tuned against, so figures on it are in-sample (`docs/INDEX.md`).

**held-out set**{: #term-held-out-set } — validation cases reserved for one decision and not consulted for any threshold; `validation-cases-heldout.tsv` is spent, `-heldout-2.tsv` is current (`docs/INDEX.md`).

**bench panel**{: #term-bench-panel } — a per-strain wet-lab result table read from a paper into `docs/bench-panels/*.tsv`, used as sensitivity and specificity evidence for scoring changes (`docs/INDEX.md`, `config.yaml scoring:`).

**design era**{: #term-design-era } — how much sequence existed when an [assay](#term-assay) was designed versus now (`records_before_design`, `records_now`, fold increase), from `scripts/design_era.py` into `docs/design-era.tsv` (`docs/INDEX.md`).

**predict protocol**{: #term-predict-protocol } — `source.predict_protocol`, the `P-0nn` protocol under which an entry's oligos were extracted (`schema.py` `Source`).

## Resolved from the repo on 2026-10-29

**tier-2 (validation)**{: #term-tier-2 } — retrospective validation: assays with published follow-up (a paper, erratum or redesign reporting the [assay](#term-assay) failing or still working on particular lineages), asked whether AssayWatch flags what the literature found using only records deposited before that paper; scored as a confusion matrix with Jeffreys intervals by `scripts/retrospective.py` (`ROADMAP.md` "[Tier](#term-tier) 2: retrospective validation"). No tier-1 is named anywhere; the word survives from the original plan's numbering.

**ground truth**{: #term-ground-truth } — a documented outcome for an ([assay](#term-assay), [lineage](#term-lineage)) pair from a [tier-2](#term-tier-2) case or a [bench panel](#term-bench-panel) row; a flag with "no ground truth either way" is one no paper or panel has judged (`config.yaml scoring:`).

**evaluable / assessable / coverage gap**{: #term-evaluable-assessable-coverage-gap } — three thresholds on one count. A record is *evaluable* as defined under **[evaluable record](#term-evaluable-record)** above. A [lineage](#term-lineage) is *assessable* when it has at least `lineage.min_records_per_lineage` evaluable records. A *coverage gap* is an assay-level shortfall below `drift.min_records_for_coverage`. Same denominator, three places it is tested.

**undecided**{: #term-undecided } — the set of drift statuses that are not a [verdict](#term-verdict): `insufficient data`, `no recent data`, `no data` (`scripts/retrospective.py UNDECIDED`). `drift.py STATUS_ORDER` carries the first two and `NO_DATA` the third; the report grays all three. `no recent data` means nothing new was deposited in the [window](#term-window); `insufficient data` means too few [evaluable](#term-evaluable-assessable-coverage-gap) records; `no data` means no [archive](#term-archive) at all.

**C1 / C2 / C3**{: #term-c1-c2-c3 } — the three layers of `docs/bayesian-scoring-plan.md`: C1 the drift proportion (replaces [Wilson](#term-wilson-newcombe-interval)/Newcombe and the flag rule), C2 the per-record [call](#term-call) (replaces the additive [penalty](#term-penalty) table), C3 the validation matrix intervals (replaces point sensitivity). The **S ladder** (`docs/journal/2026-10-24-scoring-strategy-test-plan.md`, S0 [baseline](#term-baseline), S3b, S7, S7b…) is a sequence of candidate *scoring rules* inside C2's territory, each pre-registered with kill criteria. C-numbers name what is modeled; S-numbers name one tested change to the penalty rule.

**retrospective families**{: #term-retrospective-families } — the phrase families that `scripts/find_retrospective_cases.py` uses to find citing papers (`docs/journal/2026-10-26-retrospective-case-search.md`): `miss`, a paper reporting the [assay](#term-assay) missing samples (the scarce `fails` kind, or a clinical sensitivity report); `weakened`, [reduced](#term-reduced) or [partial](#term-partial) [detection](#term-detection); `mismatch`, a paper locating [primer](#term-primer) mismatches against a [lineage](#term-lineage) (the best route to a `drift` case); `redesign`, a group redesigning the assay, which usually says why; `use`, opt-in, a paper that simply uses the assay and so may test our oligos on new material (`docs/journal/2026-10-29-use-family-cases.md`); `late_redesign`, opt-in and pre-registered, a redesign published five or more years after the design paper, the first source tried for a `drift` case (`docs/journal/2026-10-30-redesign-family.md`).

**lineage Modes A, B, C**{: #term-lineage-modes-a-b-c } — the three ways a record is assigned to a [sublineage](#term-sublineage) (`assaywatch/lineage.py` docstrings). Mode A: by taxid, when NCBI already distinguishes the sublineages below the query taxon (Avipoxvirus: fowlpox vs canarypox). Mode B: by a [title token](#term-title-token) regex (influenza subtype `(H5N1)`). Mode C: by a sequence cluster label from `assaywatch/subcluster.py` (Bd BdGPL vs BdCAPE). Each returns None to defer to the next.

## Words with more than one meaning

Each of these is one word doing several jobs. Qualify it every time.

**status**{: #term-status-3 } — registry status (`active`, `draft`, `deprecated`) or drift status (`declining`, `stable`, ...).

**flag**{: #term-flag-2 } — a [review flag](#term-review-flag) (`needs_review`) or a drift flag (the rule that puts an [assay](#term-assay) below threshold).

**verdict**{: #term-verdict } — a drift status, or under the serial [engine](#term-engine) an [oligo verdict](#term-oligo-verdict) (`ok`, `weak`, `blocked`).

**coverage**{: #term-coverage-2 } — four things: the [coverage map](#term-coverage-map) (this glossary's "Coverage" section); the drift status `low coverage`; a [coverage gap](#term-evaluable-assessable-coverage-gap) (too few records, `drift.min_records_for_coverage`); and how completely an [archive](#term-archive) was retrieved (`retrieve.py`, `composition.coverage_*`). Unqualified, it means the coverage map.

**site**{: #term-site-2 } — a binding site (`match.py`, `sitedrift.py`), or the project website (`site.py`, `site_render.py`, `site_svg.py`).

**window**{: #term-window } — [3' window](#term-3-window), [mid window](#term-mid-window), [mispair window](#term-mispair-window) (positions on a [primer](#term-primer)); [recent window](#term-recent-window) (deposit dates); [window archive](#term-window-archive) and [composition window](#term-composition-window) (stretches of a record).

**target**{: #term-target-2 } — the [assay](#term-assay)'s taxon and gene. The sequence being searched is a **record**, and the base a [primer](#term-primer) faces is the **template** base; neither is "the target".

**tier**{: #term-tier } — a [degeneracy](#term-degeneracy) tier (`negligible`, `moderate`, `high`) or [tier-2](#term-tier-2) validation.

**panel**{: #term-panel-2 } — a `Panel` in the registry schema (the paper's own [inclusivity](#term-inclusivity) counts), a [bench panel](#term-bench-panel) (`docs/bench-panels/`), or a panel of the website dashboard.

**assessable**{: #term-assessable } — a drift [lineage](#term-lineage) with enough [evaluable](#term-evaluable-assessable-coverage-gap) records; `not assessable` is a [coverage cell](#term-coverage-cell) with no locus-present record.

**round**{: #term-round } — a nested round (round 1, round 2), or the arithmetic `round()` in code.

**exclusion / exclusivity**{: #term-exclusion-exclusivity } — an exclusion is why a record yielded no [amplicon](#term-amplicon); exclusivity is a paper's claim about off-target taxa.

## Words not to use

**hit**{: #term-hit } — not a project term. An [oligo](#term-oligo) matching a record is a **site**; an [assay](#term-assay)'s outcome on a record is a **[call](#term-call)**; a record returned by a search is a **record**.

**alert**{: #term-alert } — not a project term. An assay-level statement is a **drift status** or a **[coverage cell](#term-coverage-cell)**; the rule behind a drift status is a **flag**.

**strain**{: #term-strain } — not a unit this project groups by. Say **species** (a [coverage row](#term-coverage-row)), **[lineage](#term-lineage)** or **[sublineage](#term-sublineage)**. `strain` survives only as a GenBank record qualifier.

**clade, stratum**{: #term-clade-stratum } — say **[lineage](#term-lineage)** or **[sublineage](#term-sublineage)**. The one exception is **[diverged stratum](#term-diverged-stratum)**, defined above.

**product**{: #term-product } — say **[amplicon](#term-amplicon)**.

**undetermined (record base)**{: #term-undetermined } — say **[ambiguous](#term-ambiguous)**.

**inclusivity**{: #term-inclusivity } — say **coverage**, except when naming a paper's own inclusivity panel.

**drift (for a species the assay never detected)**{: #term-drift-2 } — that is a `predicted fail` [coverage cell](#term-coverage-cell) or a `low coverage` drift status. Drift is a fall over time.
